- PRESS NOTE . 4 


Dutca 9-1-51. 
The question how far the provisions of Article 280 (1) and (2 ) of the Consti 
tution have affected the scheincs for levy of Sales Tax in the States has been under 
.consideration of both the stufe und Central ( invernments. In its Judgement in the 
State of Bombay Versus the United Motory ( India ) Limit.d, the Supreme Court 
hold that in respect of inter -state transactions only the State where the grounds are 
delivered and consumed would be competent 10 levy Sales Tax . This judgoruont les 
brought oertain * categories of inter - state transur tious with tho taxing powers of 
State Governments , and the Government of Madras lievo decided to levy sulis tax 
po such transaction with retrospective offeet from 1-4-53 the date on whuck the 
Bupreme Court delivered its judgement and to foreg ) tho levy prior to thut date . 
This quostiva how the evident hardship and inconvenience likely to be caused cu 


238 
MANIPUR GAZETTE , FEBRUARY 84, 44 


the trade by such turation could be alleviated has bone hylly gone into by this 
Government and the Central thovernment. It will allo spcently discomed by 6 . 
Corumittee of Officials , representing the Central and State Governmenta . And pending 
consideration by the State Governmont of a permanent solution for this problem , 
certain interim arrangements have been deoided upon . The Government of: Madras 
have generally accepted those arrangements and they shall be deemed to have come 
into force so far as the State of Madras is concerned on and from 1-1-54 . The 
interins arrangements aro stated below : 

• All non - resident dealers who become liable to sales tax with reference to the 
Supreme Court judgement shall submit once in evory quærter returns in respect of 
inter -state trunsactions pertaining to the Madras Stute . Such returns shall be sub 
mitad luy post in . Form ( to be prescribed / and shall be noconipanied by a 
declaration furnished by the purchasing dealer in this state to whom serially 
numbered und authenticated fornus of declaration . will be issued in triplicate for 
the purpose . The returns should be subnuitted to such authorit.y or authorities as 
will be specificed by this Stute and who will deal with all non -resident dualors , 
Buch authority or authorities shall assess the transactions of the porresident dealer 
and if necessary , before makin ; the assossment, examine the dealer s focounts at 
the bead -quarters of the Sales Tax Officer concerned in the State of the dealer s re 
sidence . The Sales Tax authorities of the dealor s State will also verify in the courso 
of their inspection of the dealer s acoounts whether any exports to other states have 
been made and if so , furnish the relevente information to the State entitled to tux 
such transactions . All final appeals against the order " of assessment and all procee 
dings involving the exercise of revisional jurisdiction will be heard , and dealt with 
at the nornul headquartors of the Authority in this state in whom such appellato 
or revisional powers vest . All the earlier appeals will be heard at the request of 
the dealer at one or more central places in the State of the dealer s residence . The 
tax due from non -resident dealers may be paid by crossed cheques , postul orders , 
or deinand drafts and not necessarily at the treasuries in this tato. 

This forms in which the returns and declarations should be submitted will be 
published in the Fort St. George Gazette in due course ,

T. Kipgen ,

RESOL TIO N. 


The Government of India have been giving careful consideration to the problem 
of the States which are constituent units of the Indian Umuul. These Studios , as 
they exist today , are largely the result of historical processes and the spread and 
consolidation of the British Power in India . On the uttuinment of independence , 
India was partitioned and the independent State of Pakistan was created . A 

pror (" 58 
of merger and integration took place in regard to whut were then called the Indiser 
States " . This integration of the old ludian States , which was brought about within 
a very short period , was au event of historic significance . The integration , however, 
was naturally based to a large extent on the old patterns which existed beſoro 
independence . 

2. The pattern of States in the Union is thus the result of luistorical accident 
and circumstances . Their mere existence for a hundred years or more developed 
political, administrative and cultural associations within and between them . 

3. The greater development of political consciousness imions the people and the 
growing importance of the great regional languages led gradually to demands for 
the formution of certain States on linguistic basis . Euch such separate probleem 
was lowover closely inter- related with other problem , and inny furmation of a new 
state necessarily affected a number of other States . It thus became increasingly 
difficult to consider any such problem in isolation . 

4. The language and culture of an area have an unduubted portance as they 
represent & pattern of living which is common in that area . In considering a re 
organisation of States , however , there aru other important factors which have also 
to be borne in mind . The first cssential consideration is the preservation and streng 
thening of the unity and seourity of India . Financial, economic and wurmistrativo 
considerations are almost equally important , not only from the promt of view of euch 
state , but for the wholu natiun . India has embarked 1 :011 is great orderedd plan 
for her economic, cultural and moral progress . Changes · whicle mterfere with the 
successful presecution of such a national plan would be harmful tu the national 
interest . 

5. The Government of India have come to the conclusion that the whole question 
of the reorganisation of the States of the Indian C mon should be carefully extincd, 
objectively and dispassionately , so that the welfare of the people of each cousutuent 
unit , as well as of the nation as a whole , in promoted . The Guvernment have accor 
dingly decided to appoint i Comuússion to conduct such un culinalon . 

6. The Commission will consist of Shri Suiyid Fazl Ali, at present Governor of Orissa , 
Shri Hriday Nath Kupzru , Dember of the Council of States, and Suri havalim Machova 
Panikkar, at present Ambassador of India in Egypt, of whorn Shri Suyid Fazl Ali 
shall be the Chairman of the Commission . 

7. The Commission will investigate the conditions of the problem , the hustorical 
background , the existing situation and the bearing of all important and relevant 
factors thereon . They will be free to consider any proposal relating to such rcor 
ganisation . The Government expect that the Conmission would , in the first instance , 
pot go into the details , but make recommednations in regard to t . s broad principlus 


252 


MANIPUR GAZETTE , MARCH 31 , 1934 . 


which should govern the solution of this problem and , if they bo choose , the broad linss 
ou which particular Status should be reorganised , and submit interiin reports for the 
considuration of Government. 

8. The Conumission will be at liberty to devise their own procedure for their work , 
for collecting torniation and for ascertaining public opinion . The Commission will 
ordinarily hold their wittings in private. 

9. The Commission will have a Secretray and such staff and advisers as may bo 
considered necessibly . 

19. The Commission will make their recommendations to the Goverument as soon 
as muy be practicable , and not later than the 30th June, 1965 .

SUGGESTIONS 


Wo are of the opinion that there are only two alteroatives to solvo 
tho problems- be being that the State of Manipur le delimited so duublo 
member constituenoy with reservation of one seat for the tributs . Whetber 
this proposal is agreeable undor tho oxisting circumstances in a matter of 
conjecture . All the more, this should be such a matter which must be de 
cided upon in deference to the ošajority and representative opinions of tbo 
tribals . And the other being that the State of Manipur ha 

State of Manipur ha devided into 
two single mom ber constituencies to be called Valloy ( oustituency and Hill 
Constituency- each respectively comprising the valley and the hill areur , 
with littio emphasis on the inequalities of the population in the respective 
constituencies, whiob , it is believed , will be quite in confonance with the spirit 
and object of the Peoples Representation Act, 1952, under which Manipur bas 
leen alloted two seats . Under the existing circumstances wo profer the 
latter to the former and recommend the latter .

Imphul, the 26th April, 1951. 
No Tax /51/53A / 100.-- The following Press Nute issued by the Goverument of 
Hyderabad is republished below for general information : 


PRESS NOTE . 


Dated 5th February , 1954. 
Even since the Hyderabad General Sules Tax Act, 1950 came into force ( 1-5-1950), 

question whether Article 286 (1) and, Lof the Constitution of India empowers 
the importing State where the goods have actually been delivered for the purpose 
of ponsumption in the State to impose tax on the inter -State trausuctions has been 
in danbt. This has been cleared by the Suprenie Court of India in its judgment 
dehered in the case of the State of Bombay vs. the United Motors (India) Ltd. 


290 


0 


MANIPUR GAZETTE , MAY 19 , 1954 . 


In view of the doubt that existed till clarified by the Supreme Court the Goverduieut 
of Ilyderabad luve decided to collect tax on the inter - Siate transactions from the 
first day of April, 1953 only , in accordance with the following procedure . (But suck 
dealers who have actually collected tax between the 1st May, 1950 and the 31st 
Murch, 19533 on inter-Stute transactions will, however, be required to pay over the 
amounts so collecteil, to the Government.) 

All non - resident dealers who are liable to pay tax shall submit once in every 
quarter , returns in respect of inter-State transactions pertaining to the State of 
Hydcrubud by post in the form prescribol by the Hyderabad , Government. The 
returns should be submitted to the Sales Tax Officer, Central Circle , Hyderabad, who 
will assess the inter- State transactious of all non - residint dealers. The Sales Tax 
Officer, Central Circle , if he feels it necessary , will examinu the accounts of the non 
l esident dealer at the lead - quarters of the Sales Tax Officer concerned in the State 
of the dealer s residence . 

Appeals arising out of such diesessments muy, at the request of the dealer , lo 
heard at one or two central places in the State of the dealer s residence. All 
proceedings involving the jurisdiction of the Revisional Authority would , however, 
bu dealt with at the normal Head -quarters of the Revisional Authority in this State 
( llyderabad City ) 

The tax due from the non - resident dealers shall be paid by either crossed choquos 
or postal orders or demnand drafts in favour of the Sales Tax Officer, Central Circle ,

Imphal, the 10th June , 1954 . 
The Indian Boilers Act, 1928 lays down that all bpilars exceeding 6 gallons in 
capacity should be registered in accordance with the provisious of the Act. An instance 
has been brought to the notice of the Government of Medras iawhich , Builer was 
supplied by a mannfacturing firm in Ludhunain to a purchaser in the State of Madras, 
with in - correct intimation that its cupacity was less than ive gallons and that it 
did not therefore come under the purview of the Indian Boileru Apt On exami 
nation by the Madras Boilor Inspectorate it was found that the Boiler was not 
offered for registrations and even if it was offered it could not be registered under 
the Indian Bullers Act 1923 , as its construction was not in conformity with the stan 
dard condition laid down for registration of Bojlers . 

Any person who possesses any boilers of the kind mentioned above is therefore 
advised to refrain from using them unless and until they have been duly registored 
under the Act , failing which they will be liable for promevution under the Act . It 
is also necessary that when purchases of suoh boilers of marginal capacity Aro 
templated , the intending purchasers should consult the Chief Inspector of Boilers, 
Assum (who is the Chief Inspector of Boilers , Manipur also ) to ensure that the Boilera 
do not come under the Indian Boilers Act 1923 and if they do , the materials and 
the construction of the Boilers conform to the Indian Boiler : Rogulations 400 
will be acceptable for purposes of registration under the Indian Boilers, Act .

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS 
The Indian Arms Act of 1880 was substituted by the lodina Arms Act of 18 
without any substantial modifications. It has practically continued unaltered evi 
ofter India has attained freedom . It is imperatively necesy that the restuctio 
relating to arms be so relaxed as to bring our arms laws in conformity with thu 
af other frue nations. It is essential that as far as possible, efforts should be nia 

to liberalise the Indian Arms Act , 1878 or the rules made thereunder for the purpu 
cof allowing certain categories of peaceful citizens, in the Aposte instance , to have arı 
for self defenpe . The Bull bas therefore been prenanted in this form . 

It has also been provided that rules framed by Government from time to tu 
should be laid on the tables of both the House of Parliamant .

This , the third instalment of the Hindu Coda , och kan lo amend and codily the lens 
rolating to intestate succession . The originul draft of the provisions relating 
intestato succession contained in the Run Cunmittee s Bill unde went substantial 
changes in the hunds of the Select Committee which considered the Ran Committees 
Bill in 1948. This Bill follows to a large extent the schema uopted lis the Select 
Committee but takes into account tbe various suggestions utiles from time to time

Notes on cloruar 
Clause 1. Like the Hindu Marriage and Divorce Bill and the Ilindu Minority 
and Guardianship Bill, this law also will have extraterritorial effect . 

Clauser 2 and 4. These clauses are and will be a common feuture of all Bills 
relating to Hindu law . 

Clause 3 .--- The expression " related " is so defined that the rights of illegitimate 
children are safexuarded as against their mother and their own legitimate descendants . 
This definition follows the Rau Coinmittee s draft where it is pointed out that to 
confine relutionship to ligitimate kinship mijht prevent a Naikin s property from 
passing to her son or daughter and that there is also no reason why Naikin s chil 
dren should not have mutual rights of inheritance. 

The question of domicile becomes relevant with respect to clause B , and domicile 
is deterinined by the usual rules applicable thereto as laid down in sections to 
18 of the Indian Succession Act , 1925 . 

Clause 6. - This clause excludes from the application of this law joint- family property 
which under the Mitakshara law devolves on heirs by the rule of survivorship and 
property to which the Indian Succession Act , 1925 , applies by mouson of a 
marriage having taken place under the Special Marriage Act, 1872. It also excludes 
estates which are in their nature or by custom impartible . 

Clause 6.- This clause lays down the well-known principles which apply to regulate 
Buc.cession to the movable and immovable properties of an intestate. (Compare section 
B of the Indian Succession Act , 1925 ) . 

Cluse 7.-- Under the existing Hindu law , rules of succession exist whereby 
reunited son may be preferred to a son who remains separate; a maiden daughter 
may be preferred to & murriet daughter ; us between married daughters , « married 
daughter who is indigent may be preferred to a married daughter who is possessed 
of meads and so In view of the scheme of Bucocasion adopted in the Bill , 
these distinctions have necessarily to be ruled ont . 

Clauses 8 to 10 .-- Before 1937 , the " simultaneous beirs " of a male Hindu dying intes 
tate coniprised only the son , the son of a pre deceased son and the son of a pro deceased nou 
of a pre -deceased son . The Hindu Women s Rights to Property Act, : 937, added to the 
list the widows of the first two as well as the intestate s own widow . Class I of ih , prafe 
rential beirs in the Schedule now adds to the existing list of simultaneous heirs , 
the daughter , and further seeks , as far as possible , to traat the other grandchildren 
of an intestate , whose pare.it has pro-deceased , the intestate , on the same footing 
as the son of u pre -deceased son , except that in the former case the share to be 
divided among the children will be less than in the latter 0480 .

neous succession , like father and mother , brother and sister and so on . The number

PRESS NOTE . 

DECONTROL OF RICE , 
Reports have been received that there is some confusion in certain quarters 
that movement 

of rice from one place to another would not be free till Stato 
Gorcruments issue necessary notifications withdrawing the restrictions that they had 
imposed on the movement of rive under the powers vested in theru . T he Govera 
dent of India wish to clarify that tbe notification issued by them cancels ull 
restrictions imposed by the State Goverpments - on movement of rice and these 
restrictions become null and void with effect from July 10 , 1954. From that date 
the movement of rice from onu State to another is absolutely free . 

T he Government of India have issued instructions to State Governments for 
giving wocesory publicity to this clarification througbout their jurisdiction .

Subject :- Acceptance of Government Promissory Notes of 31 : National Plan Loun, 

1904 48 Security from coutractors . 
TM - 2 / 34 / 54 /56 . Attention of all Central lleuds of Departments is drawn to 
rule 277 (ii) of the General Financial Rules, which permits the acceptance of secu 
rity from contractors, Government oflicials etc., in the form of Government pruiuis 
sory Notes . Doubts have been raised whether investments in the Nationul I lum 
Loan , would be acceptablo as Security . Now , it has been decried by the Govem 
ment of India , Ministry of Finance , that investments in the National Plan Iwan 
in the form of Government Promissory Notes come within the perviow of rulo 
277 (ü ) of the G. F. R. and therefore cun be accepted as security .

No. J/ 23 /53. --The following Ordinance promulated by thu President is ropu 
blished below for general information : 
THE PRESS ( OBJECTIONABLE MATTER ) AMENDMENT ORDINANCE , 1954 


No. 4 OF 1954 


An Ordinance to amend the Press ( Objectionable Matter ) Act , 1951. 

WHELLAS A Bill to umeul the Press ( Objectionable Matter ) Act , 1951, bas 
been introduced in Pyrliament but has not yet been pas ed ; 

AND WHEREAS Parliament is not in session and the President is satisfied that 
circunstances exist which render it necess ir ! for him to take immediate active to 
give effout to the amendments proposed in the said Bill ; 

Now , THEREFORE , in exercise of the power, conferred by clause (1 ) of article 
123 of the Constitution , the President is pleised a promulgate the following

Under Article 27 of the Constitution of India , as interpreted by the Supremo 
Court iu State of Bunubny i erstly United Motors ( lodia ) Ltd., Bombay , lovy of 
sales tax is permissible by the importing State un certain transnotious of an inter 
State nature . The liability on such transactions arises frora January 26 , 1950 . 
Tho U. P. Guvrement . huwavur , 

1116usuru of conoessiou to dowlers , decided 
uut to give re110- poctive etteot the Supreme Court s decision , but to levy 
tax on such transactions from April 1, 1953, to tho extent permissible under the 
U. P. Salos Tact . 

2. It los . Wow bi ( n representid tu Government that the ex . U. P. dealers 
generally can to know of their liability to pay U. P. Sales tax such inter 
Stute tru uctions considerably after delivery of the judgment of tbe Suprenie 
Court . Tils did not, during this period , realise auy tax from their constituants 
and it whild , therefore CHUHE them great hardship it tax is now charged from 
them from April 1, 1053. 

3. Government have carefully considered this representation . They are of tho 
opinion hat there is no legal justification for advancing the date from which tax 
is to by charged beyond April 1, 1953. In order , howover, to advoid hardship 
to dealı y who may not have charged sales tax as such , they buvo now deoided 
to advice this dato to January , 1, 1954 , in the case of only those dealors who

PRESS NOTE No. 72 


Dated , the 20th October, 1951 . 
In press Communique No. 2 dated 10th June 1964 the non -resident dowlers 
were informed that tboy should submit the roturas ( in form A -3A ) for the quarters 
ending June 30 , 1963, September 30 , 1963, and December 31, 1963 ou or before 
June 16 , 1964 , and for the quarter ending Maroh 91, 1954 before Juge 30 , 1964 , 
and that they should apply for licences for the years 1953-84 und 1984-85 and 
for registration for the year 1953-54 , on or before June 15 , 1956. Subsequently 
with reference to certain representations received from the Mysore Chamber of 
Commerce , thus Government in their Press Communique No. 3, dated 27th July 
1984 extendud the time limit for filing the several returns by 200 -resident dealers 
till 318t July 1954 . 

It has been represented that only a few non - resident dealers bad applied for 
registration and licences and submitted turnover returns within the prescribed date , 
namely 31st July 1984. It bas also been pointed out that there are still a large 
number of uon- resideut dealers wbo have yet to register theonelves , apply for 
licences , and submit turnover returns. As the orders staad at prosent , penal notion 
can be taken for late registration and late submission of turnover returns. In the 
case of licences , applications , for licences for 1953-54 received after 318 July 1954 
were liable to be rejected . In order to avoid bardabir to the non -readent doulon 
the Government extond as a special case , the time for submitting applications 
for licences kod registration and the quarterly returns by non -rasident dealers till 
the 16th November , 1964. The Government howovor ,wish to make it clear that 
unless the non - resident dealers avail themselves of this opportunity and submit 
the applications for registration and licences and also ile the quarterly roturas 
proboribed within the period aforesaid , they will not be eligible for lioonces in the 
Case of commodities taxable at concessional rates, and that penal action will be 
taken against them for non -registration and non -submission of roturtu .

PRESS NOTE . 


REPUBLIC DAY TO BE A PAID HOLIDAY. 
In pursuance of instructions issued by the Central Ministry of Labour ou previous 
anniversaries of the Republic Day , workers were permitted to participate in the 
celebration of January , 20 without being made to suffer any loss in wages. 

A similar directivo has been issued this year by the Government of India 
to their officer B in charge of industrial underlakings and they bope that other 
employers as well will co -operate with them by deolaring this national day as a paid 
boliday . 

In view of the great importance of the occasion , Government presume that many 
industrial undertakings have already prescribed January, 26 as one of their regular 
holidays 

but where this liay uot buon done , thoy hope employers will truat tbe 
day 18 an additioval paid holiday and not as a substitutes holiday . 

Ministry of Labour

PRESS RELEASE NO . fi 


Imphal, the 18th Feb., 1965 . 
1. Unruly moby organised by the P.S.P. are continuin ; to block the Dimapur 
Road and obstruct trattio . Mobile police parties are doing their best to clear 
the roads by persuading poby to move way . In some CAHOS individual 
police men have been attucked . So far the police have contined themselves 
to pushing the pur80118 uway from the rold or using mild lathi charge to 
olear them but there is is growing teudenvy on the part of the groups to 
attempt to snatch the lutbis from the police and to throw stones at thunu 
and the police lay therefore be constrained to use more effective methods 
if the situation persiste . In some cases the obstruction is buy pla ing laryo 
stopoy or trues across the road . 

2. Justice Deka of the Assam High Court who is the Chairman of the 
Advisory Board appointed under the Preventive Detention Act to examinu 
the cases of dentortion of certain P.S.P. leaders in the State arrived in 
Imphal on the oth by road from Gaubuti along the Dimapur Kond . His 
our W83 alou obstructod on the road by a P.S.P. group 40 miles froin Imphal. 

3. This Administration wishox to waru the poople concerned that such 
obstruction is unlawful and constitutos a source of annoyanco to the 
public and gravo danger to the public safety and that the Government is 
bound to take firm measures to doul sovorely with these inruly elements 
in the interests of public order and safety . 

4. Ou Iith February, & P.S.P. organised mob of more than 500 furcibly 
entered the S. D. O s office at Ukhrul after overpowering & cordon of police 
men and office staff and threatened to kidnap the $ .1).(). by force. They 
also pelted stones at the police and the office building and broke all window 
panes. The police triod to disperse them by * cane churge but it proved 
ineffective . As there was grave danger to tbe safety of the 8.0.0 . and bis 
staff and the policemen , the police opened fir under the orders of the S D.O. 
resulting in injury to 8 persons who are being treated in Ukhrul Hospital. 
Tho situation is since quite . The District Magistrate has visited the spot 
and held an enquiry . 

6. On account of the unsettled conditions created by the unruly orowds 
organised by the P.S.P. it has become impossible to effect payment of 
A. R. M. compensation in villages around Ukhrul where paymont had been 
programmed during the coming few days . The list of persons to whom 
compensation has been sanotioned will be published in the villages , but it 
is regretted that it will not be poasible to effect disbursement till normal 
situation is reatured ; fresh dates for disbursement will be fixed us 8.00 
as possible .

চট্রনিং লৈবিদা দুটি করােই । 

ই - নােম এগা অপুনবা ওইনা ট্রেনিংগম চােষ চৎবম দেয় এলায়েন্স দেই । 
মীংচমনা চে অমসুং অতৈ অতৈ মরােল ডিপুটিফিনান্স ফিতাআপনি ।

NOTIFICATION .

No. 7 of 1958 . 

Imphal, the 29th March , 1957 . 
In exercise of the powers conferred by Sootion 41 of the Special Marriage Act, 
1984 (Act 43 of 1934 ), the Judicial Commissioner, Manipur is pleased to frame the 
following rules for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of Chapters V , 
VI and VII of the aforesaid Act . 
These rules shall come into force immodistoly . 

By Order, 

Singh . 

Registrar, 
1. In these rules unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context 
"Court means the District Court as defined in sec . 2 cl , (e) of the Special Marriage 
Act, 1954 ( Act XLIII of 1951 ). 

" The Act " means the Special Marriage Act , 1964 ( Act XLIII of 1954). 

" Prescribed ” means prescribed by these rules . 
2. An appeal filed under ned, 8 or 17 of tho Act shall be accompanied by a 
cortified copy of the order uppealed against. As soon 

As soon ay an appeal is tiled it shall 
bo numbered according to the serial number in the prescribed register and the par 
ticulars thereof shall be entered in the same. Tho register shall be in Form No. 1 . 

3. The appellant shall filo along with the petitiou of appoal or on any subsequent 
date as the Court may direct copy os copies of the petition and autice in the 
prescribed form for service upon the Marriage Officer and any other person who 
intervened before the Marriage Officer, who passed the order appealed against. If 
any one intervened before the Marriage Oficer, the application of appeal shall state 
clearly bis name and address .
